authority.training_target: Qwen3.5-0.8B-class reusable cognitive-process substrate; runtime N variable; GRID10 benchmark-only

audited_sources.finding: The authority-pinned producer dynamically loads tools/trigger2_hyperposition_reference_labelers_v3.py and the artefact RFC8785 canonicalizer by path. The returned execution receipt binds the producer source SHA-256 and JCS digests of policy/world/prestate/event/result, but it does not bind the byte identity of those dynamically loaded executable dependencies.

Repository lineage verification is strong for the authority-declared producer path/commit/HEAD bytes, but the gate imports that producer and reconstructs with the same current transitive dependencies. No transitive executable dependency manifest/hash was observed for the labeler or canonicalizer. This permits a self-consistent moving-dependency island to remain internally reproducible while the pinned producer source itself is unchanged.

The authority binds producer source bytes and lineage plus the policy JCS digest, but no labeler-source SHA, canonicalizer-source SHA, gate-source SHA, or complete transitive execution-manifest digest was observed.

The deterministic semantic functions u_state, d_resolve, u_test_order and f_salience_order are retained, but internal _digest() uses Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'),ensure_ascii=False) rather than the repository RFC8785/JCS canonicalizer. Derivation receipts and canonical semantic-state digests are therefore deterministic in the current Python implementation but are not established as RFC8785 cross-runtime causal identities.

A repository JCS implementation already exists and explicitly implements UTF-16 property ordering, finite binary64 constraints, JCS number formatting and fail-closed signed-zero admission. The audit therefore identifies a convergence gap, not a need to invent a second canonicalization authority.

relevant_requirements: cryptographic hashes require invariant canonical representation
JSON numbers use ECMAScript-compatible binary64 serialization
object property ordering is recursive and based on UTF-16 code units

examples.implication: plain Python compact JSON is not JCS number identity
Python code-point key ordering can differ from JCS UTF-16 ordering

material_finding.statement: Pinning only the top-level A02 producer bytes is insufficient to authenticate the executable semantic derivation path because producer behavior also depends on dynamically loaded labeler and canonicalizer bytes. A gate that reconstructs with the same unpinned current dependencies can pass self-consistently after a dependency change. Exact repository HEAD/tree identity narrows the checkout but does not substitute for declaring which dependency bytes are part of the producer contract when the authority itself pins an older producer lineage.
material_finding.scope: A02 source/execution provenance and general Trigger-2 derivation identity only

secondary_finding.statement: The v3 Hyperposition reference labeler has deterministic Python-local semantic hashes but does not use the repository JCS authority for derivation/state identities. These hashes must not be treated as cross-runtime canonical causal identity until migrated or explicitly namespaced as compatibility digests.

hypothesis: A fully dependency-bound A02 execution manifest plus one canonical JCS identity path will eliminate a class of self-consistent moving-source passes without changing the intended Hyperposition semantics.
counterhypothesis: Repository HEAD/tree plus reconstructed output may be operationally sufficient for a one-language bounded pilot if every consumer binds the full checkout identity and never treats internal compact digests as portable authority. Even then, explicit dependency identity remains higher-auditability and prevents future extraction/reuse from silently losing the checkout-wide assumption.

recommended_successor_gate.receipt_requirement: Bind one JCS digest of the complete dependency manifest into the execution receipt and verify every path against executed HEAD before producer invocation.
negative_controls: mutate labeler bytes while producer bytes remain unchanged => reject before execution credit
mutate canonicalizer bytes while producer bytes remain unchanged => reject
mutate generation-authority bytes under same schema/path => reject
mutate dependency manifest after receipt generation => reject
wrong HEAD/tree with individually matching copied files => reject according to declared repository lineage policy
canonicalization_convergence: reuse the existing EntityOS RFC8785/JCS canonicalizer; do not create a second JSON identity authority
migrate reference semantic digests in a versioned successor or explicitly namespace old Python-compact hashes as compatibility-only
add RFC8785 edge regressions for binary64 formatting, signed zero policy, UTF-16 property ordering, lone surrogate rejection and exact-I-JSON integer admission
cross-check the same world/state/event through labeler and A02 identity plumbing
